stories.headline: Bihar CM reviews flood situation in Begusarai, announces measures to strengthen Ganga embankments
stories.title: Bihar CM reviews flood situation in Begusarai, announces measures to strengthen Ganga embankments
stories.summary: Choudhary arrived in Begusarai at around 3:30 pm, accompanied by Union Minister and Begusarai MP Giriraj Singh.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Choudhary arrived in Begusarai at around 3:30 pm, accompanied by Union Minister and Begusarai MP Giriraj Singh.

Amid rising water levels in the Ganga and the worsening flood situation in Begusarai, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary visited the district on Saturday to assess the situation and review ongoing relief and rescue operations.
Along with senior officials and public representatives, he visited Kailashpur Mor in Ulav to take stock of the flood-affected areas.
During the inspection, the Chief Minister sought information from officials about the prevailing flood situation, the areas affected and the relief and rescue measures being undertaken.
He directed the concerned departments to ensure that immediate assistance reaches affected residents and that all necessary administrative arrangements remain in place.
Following the field inspection, Choudhary visited the IOCL Guest House and held a review meeting with officials.
The meeting was expected to assess the availability of relief supplies, transportation, healthcare facilities, cattle fodder and other essential services in flood-affected areas.

After assessing the situation, Choudhary said around 20 lakh cusecs of water were currently flowing through the Ganga, while approximately 5.5 lakh cusecs have been released into the Sone River from the border.
“Certainly, this is a matter of concern.
However, the administration is fully alert at every location, and efforts are underway to provide all necessary facilities to the people,” the Chief Minister said.
He said steps had also been initiated towards finding a permanent solution to Bihar’s recurring flood problem.

According to Choudhary, the government had earlier focused primarily on the Kosi and Gandak rivers, but officials had now been directed to ensure that Ganga embankments were fully repaired and strengthened.

stories.headline: PM Modi's Strong Message to the World from the SCO Summit in Bishkek
stories.title: PM Modi's Strong Message to the World from the SCO Summit in Bishkek
stories.summary: FRAGRANCE OF IDEAS Prime Minister Narendra Modi was recently on a very successful four-day visit to two Central Asian nations, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. Besides attending the usual official ceremonies, bilateral meetings and other important engagements in the two countries, PM Modi also attended the two-day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. The Summit was also attended by the Russian President, Vladimir Putin and the Chinese President, Xi Jinping, besides the other heads of government that were invited to the Summit. There is no doubt in the fact that the visit of PM Modi and the SCO Summit 2026 attracted the attention of the whole world, and all these developments were duly reported and covered by the global media. The presence of the heads of the governments of China, Russia and India in Bishkek was seen with keen interest by the international media, geopolitical watchers and the Western media and political establishments. PM Modi made a very impactful presence in Tashkent-Uzbekistan during his visit there before coming to Kyrgyzstan. The talks therein were focussed on bilateral cooperation, energy issues, and regional security. The Indian side also discussed the important issue of a possible uranium supply programme in the near future to India from Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received PM Modi at the Tashkent international airport and accorded him a befitting welcome on behalf of his government. He also conferred Uzbekistan’s prestigious honour 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' (Order of Friendship) upon PM Modi in recognition of his international stature and huge positive contribution to the global cooperation. This is Modi's 36th international award, which he has received over the last 12 years globally. PM Modi also held very productive delegation-level strategic talks with the Uzbek's side during his two-day stay in Tashkent. Modi also participated in yoga programmes in Tashkent, inter-cultural events, Ramcharitmanas recitation event, interactive programmes with scholars, Indologists, youth and the students at the university and the tree-plantation ceremonies. He also visited the former Prime Minister of India Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial and paid floral tributes to his memory. It was here in Tashkent that the former PM Shastri breathed his last during the Indo-Pak talks in 1966. On reaching Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, from Tashkent, PM Modi received an impressive ceremonial welcome. He held bilateral talks with the Kyrgyzstan delegation headed by their President, Sadyr Zhaparov, to enhance bilateral economic and commercial relationship between the two nations. He also attended the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan alongside visiting global and regional leaders who had come to Bishkek in connection with the SCO Summit on 31st August and 1st September 2026. At the Summit, PM Modi made a strong plea to the world to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terror financing without double standards. He said that in the previous meeting of the SCO, he had outlined three pillars as India's vision for the SCO, and these included 'security, connectivity and opportunity'. He said, " The time has come to move these three pillars beyond vision and translate them into concrete outcomes. The first and foremost requirement for this is peace and security. Terrorism continues to pose a serious challenge to humanity as a whole. In the fight against terrorism, we cannot remain confined to an action-reaction approach. We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue. We must send a strong message to countries that use terrorism as an instrument of policy and provide safe haven and support to terrorists that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone. Our shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan. India has been contributing to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to the people of Afghanistan and will continue to do so. In today’s interconnected world, the scope of security has become even broader. The crisis in West Asia has demonstrated that a conflict in one region does not remain confined to that region. Its impact is felt across the world, affecting energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains. The countries of the Global South bear the greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on the battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy. Drug trafficking is not merely a crime; it is a serious threat to our younger generation and regional security. The Centres being established under the SCO to address challenges such as security threats, organised crime, information security, and narcotics are a positive step. We must make these Centres an effective instrument for practical coordination and timely action". On the sidelines of the Summit, PM Modi met the Russian President Vladimir Putin and urged an immediate and peaceful resolution to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. His quote got a lot of attention and appreciation that suggests; 'From endless war to the end of war'. He also met the Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to expand trade and address West Asian diplomatic stability. The President of Iran requested Modi to use his extensive resources to bring the Iran and West Asia crisis to a halt. Pezeshkian urged Modi to leverage India's extensive relationships with various international parties to help stop the cycle of violence and support a peaceful dialogue process. He also thanked India for its support and cooperation during the recent conflict and called Modi a man of peace. In a bizarre attempt to showcase his presence at the Summit, the Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharief, who was also attending the SCO Summit, committed his office to post an edited group-photograph of the leaders of the Summit on their social media handle. He did so immediately after PM Modi's office posted the original group photograph of the Summit on social media. However, due to the huge international criticism mixed with sarcasm and embarrassment, the Pakistan PMO was compelled to change the 'edited photograph ', which brought humiliation for Pakistan globally and left behind a diplomatic distaste. Additionally, Sharief, in his address, raked up the issue of the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) at the SCO summit unsuccessfully. However, the External Affairs Ministry of India, under the leadership of Dr. S.Jay Shankar, External Affairs Minister, who was also attending the Summit, issued a befitting reply from Bishkek itself and made its stand known to the world on the IWT issue. The statement said that the Hague-based International Tribunal ruling that 'India’s decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty was not legally permissible and that the 1960 pact remains fully in force' was not in any way acceptable to India. India rejected the ruling, saying the tribunal had no jurisdiction to pronounce on its sovereign decisions. India rejected the award and also the interim measures order, reiterating that it does not recognise the Court of Arbitration and has never participated in its proceedings. “This so-called court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty; and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a frontal statement issued from Bishkek. The statement is a rejoinder to all the concerned who try to intervene in the internal affairs of a sovereign nation-state. India walked the talk very emphatically during the whole diplomatic process, pursuing its established policy doctrines, i.e. "Terror & Talks won't go together" and "Water & Blood can't flow together". India’s consistent policy in this regard has stood the test, particularly when it elaborated that as long as Pakistan abets, sponsors and supports terrorism, there can be no real and normal relationship with it. This time, even The New York Times, that keeps on criticising India's policies and PM Modi's leadership, was forced to change the line. It highlighted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's diplomatic strategy as a "hedge" against shifting U.S. trade policies under President Trump during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek. The New York Times reported that India is actively building new global partnerships and securing concrete economic and strategic deals to reduce its exposure to unpredictable U.S. trade pressures. The coverage in the paper noted that PM Modi has travelled extensively, visiting around 20 nations since August 2025, to hammer out independent economic ties, such as submarine technology cooperation with Germany and trade adjustments with European and Asian partners. The MOU signed with the European Union sometime back is a big example in this context. PM Modi's presence alongside Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Bishkek summit was framed as part of India's multi-aligned foreign policy, balancing non-Western cooperation while navigating wider global and economic tensions. Energy security, new strategic deals, long term investments, historic engagements, forging cultural ties and opening new vistas for the establishment of peace in the highly volatile conflict regions globally are the most important takeaways of PM Modi's Central Asian tour this time. The whole world now awaits the BRICS summit that is going to take place on September 12 & 13 in New Delhi under India's BRICS 2026 chairship. (The author is a senior BJP & KP leader, Human Rights Defender and columnist and can be reached at: ashwanikc2012@gmail.com )

stories.headline: PM Modi says India demonstrating its strength amidst global turmoil, hits out at naysayers
stories.title: PM Modi says India demonstrating its strength amidst global turmoil, hits out at naysayers
stories.summary: New Delhi, Sep 5: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday asserted that India is not only growing at 7.8 per cent but also creating employment opportunities despite wars and disruptions, demonstrating the country's strength, and said that those responsible for pushing the economy into the "fragile five" cannot digest it. Addressing the centenary celebrations of the Delhi University's Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), PM Modi also said that those who once spread terror have been silenced and if today Pakistan commits any misdeed, the Indian Army strikes back on their own soil. He said from Jammu and Kashmir to the Northeast, there is peace and Naxalism has been dismantled. Recalling that the country was struggling on every front in 2013, when he last addressed SRCC students as Gujarat chief minister, Modi said corruption, terrorism and inflation were unchecked, but India is now far more secure economically and socially. However, some people's frustration is increasing after seeing this, he said. "For such people, I had given a homoeopathy dose from the Red Fort (during Independence Day address)... 'dimagi Naxal'. "When I said 'dimagi Naxal', all such people came to the forefront and started criticising me. People who were promoting dimagi Naxalism, their true colour can be witnessed by the people," he said. The prime minister said the world was at that time worried about India's policy paralysis, but today they are talking about India's policy dynamism. Modi said that in other words, India is not only growing, but also creating employment opportunities. "They once called us the 'Fragile Five'. Today, they are talking about India as the fastest-growing major economy," he said He recalled that his address at SRCC in 2013 had made a "wave" and even today, 13-14 years later, its impact remains intact. "In 2013, when I came to SRCC, I presented a vision. Whatever I said back then was my conviction... I gave the example of a glass filled with water. Some people see the glass as half full... It was a time when the country was lacking hope. So I said, 'I see the glass as fully filled'," he said. "Those who saw the glass as half empty in 2013, when I had visited the SRCC, still chose to see it the same way today. "India's 7.8 per cent growth has also come at a time when the war in West Asia is ongoing and when disruptions related to trade have persisted. Achieving such growth during that time demonstrates India's strength," he said, referring to GDP growth rate for April-June quarter. "We all know that those responsible for pushing India into the 'fragile five' cannot digest the numbers of India’s growth," he said in a veiled attack at the Congress and its allies that have questioned the credibility of the growth figures. The prime minister said in the past six years, the country has faced many challenges, be it COVID or the conflicts in West Asia, and every time, it was said that PM Modi would not be able to survive these challenges. "But India has such immense capability that the wishes of those who want to see India fail are repeatedly being left unfulfilled," he said. Referring to his 2013 visit to SRCC, just before becoming the prime minister of India, Modi said that 13 years ago, the seniors of the present generation of students could not dream of doing many things, but today, the current generation is dreaming big because India has created the ecosystem to achieve those dreams. "I am happy that you are all ambitious. Ambition comes from the environment around you. Today, you talk about start-ups, becoming entrepreneurs and bringing innovation to agriculture," he said. Outside the campus, the prime minister said, the students will find two types of people--"those who positively transform the power of society into the power of the nation and the others who turn into angry uncles (naraz fufa) as soon as any work begins". He said such "negative people's favourite activity is to oppose every task and they have just one dialogue - 'What is the need for this' ". The prime minister said in 2013, when he talked about 'Make in India', people in that ecosystem thought it was not possible, and they still mock 'Make in India'. "But now, you are witnessing the brand value of Make in India. Today, every person has a smartphone. Made in India smartphones are reaching every corner of the world. In 2014, India used to import mobile phones. Today, India is exporting mobile phones worth more than Rs 2.5 lakh crore," he said. Modi said India will have its own space station, and everyone will witness that day too. "When India one day hosts such Olympics that the world will be left in awe. These are not mere words; these are resolutions, and work is underway in the country to turn these resolutions into reality," he said. The prime minister said that earlier most things for India's armed forces were bought from abroad, but he worked with the country's armed forces to make a plan, prepared a list of items and told Indian companies to manufacture all of them. "Today, the country's defence manufacturing is at an all-time high. Today, India is producing defence goods worth nearly two lakh crore rupees. In 2013-14, we used to do defence exports worth 600-700 crore rupees; today, this figure has reached nearly Rs 40,000 crore rupees," he said. Lauding SRCC for shaping generations, PM referred to college alumni as "OG", striking a chord with Gen Z. "When a human being lives for 100 years, they are considered a person of deep knowledge and great experience. When an institution completes 100 years, it becomes an ocean of achievements. SRCC has shaped generations and connected them to a brighter future. "In its 100-year journey, Shri Ram College of Commerce has shaped generations, connecting them to a bright future. Those who came, they studied; those who left, they left sculpted. SRCC alumni have been very special. In your language, they are OGs," he said. The prime minister also released a commemorative Rs 100 coin to mark the centenary celebration. Modi's visit to the SRCC comes amid the BJP's ongoing outreach to the young generation. In April this year, the prime minister met the governing body and a delegation from the college at his residence to mark the institution's 100th anniversary. He also released a special commemorative postage stamp on the occasion.

stories.headline: Eight HC chief justices appointed
stories.title: Eight HC chief justices appointed
stories.summary: New Delhi, Sep 5: Eight high court chief justices were appointed on Saturday, days after their names were recommended by the Supreme Court Collegium. In a post on X, Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said Justice Valluri Kameswar Rao, currently a judge of the Delhi High Court, has been appointed Chief Justice of the Patna High Court. Justice Ravindra V Ghuge of the Bombay High Court will head the Calcutta High Court. Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal of the Chhattisgarh High Court has been appointed Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, while Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi of the Allahabad High Court has been appointed Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. A controversy erupted following serious, unprecedented allegations levelled against Rajasthan acting chief justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma by Supreme Court judge Sandeep Mehta. Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has been appointed Chief Justice of the court. Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra of the Orissa High Court has been appointed Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court. Justice Alpesh Yeshwant Kogje of the Gujarat High Court will head the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati of the Rajasthan High Court has been appointed Chief Justice of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court wants affidavit on IPS postings in CAPFs, continues oversight of 2025 judgment
stories.title: Supreme Court wants affidavit on IPS postings in CAPFs, continues oversight of 2025 judgment
stories.summary: In an affidavit, the Union Home Secretary had informed the court that 46 IPS officers have been brought on deputation to the CAPFs up to the SAG level after the court’s 2025 judgment
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court’s order in the Central Armed.
Police Forces (CAPF) cadre case, uploaded on Saturday (September 5, 2026), specifically asks Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan to explain the procedure followed for bringing Indian.

Police Service (IPS) officers on deputation to the CAPFs, including whether the borrowing organisations had made formal requisitions, and the reasons for making such appointments despite the court’s earlier direction to progressively reduce IPS deputation posts up to the Senior Administrative Grade level.
The court said that it “shall continue monitoring of implementation of the judgment” dated May 23, 2025.

On September 2, while hearing a contempt petition filed by former CAPF officers regarding the non-implementation of the top court’s 2025 order to progressively reduce IPS deputation in CAPFs up to the rank of Inspector Generals in the next two years, the court had sought an explanation from Mr. Mohan.
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan had orally observed that there was a “strong lobby” and the cadre officers of CAPFs were completely stifled.

On Saturday (September 5), the order uploaded by the Bench of Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S. Chandurkar, said: “Before we pass necessary order(s), we direct the Secretary to the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs to explain the above statement, for bringing in IPS officers on deputation to the five CAPFs; what procedure was followed before bringing the above officers on deputation i.e., whether any requisition was made by the borrowing department for deputation etc. and the reasons for bringing them on deputation notwithstanding the judgment of this court directing that the number of posts earmarked for deputation in the cadres of the CAPFs up to the level of SAG should be progressively reduced over a period of time, say within an upper limit of two years.”
In an affidavit, the Union Home Secretary had informed the court that 46 IPS officers have been brought on deputation to the CAPFs up to the SAG level after the court’s 2025 judgment.
The court has directed the Home Secretary to file an affidavit within two weeks detailing the procedure followed for bringing the officers on deputation.
According to the affidavit, the Border Security Force (BSF) received 13 IPS officers, Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) 11, the Central Reserve.
Police Force (CRPF) nine, the Indo-Tibetan Border.
Police (ITBP) six and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) seven officers.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to launch monthly lecture series on law, justice & legal education
stories.title: Supreme Court to launch monthly lecture series on law, justice & legal education
stories.summary: First edition of series to be held in September 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: To create a regular platform for dialogue and exchange of ideas on important contemporary issues concerning law, justice and society, the Supreme Court of India, in first of its kind initiative, announced a monthly lecture series on law, justice and legal education and also proposed an annual award.
On the occasion of Teacher's Day, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant announced on Saturday that the top court is set to launch a monthly lecture series on law, justice and legal education.
"It will create a regular platform for dialogue and exchange of ideas on important contemporary issues concerning law, justice and society.
Built around the idea of "One important idea.

Every month", the series will bring together the Bench, Bar, academia, eminent experts and young legal minds to engage with questions that are relevant to the legal system as well as to society at large.
The initiative is envisaged as a continuing intellectual platform of the Supreme Court of India," a statement issued by the apex court said.
It further said that the chief justice of India will guide the themes, speakers and overall format of the series, with each edition focusing on a contemporary and significant subject.
The series will feature a lecture followed by dialogue, under which each monthly edition will feature a distinguished lecture by an eminent jurist, scholar, legal educationist or domain expert.
"The focused lecture will seek to explain the chosen subject with clarity, authority and practical relevance.

The lecture will be followed by an ideas dialogue — a moderated discussion that will also provide an opportunity for selected questions and participation from young advocates, law students and researchers," the statement said.

It added that the series will seek to go beyond a conventional lecture format by encouraging informed discussion across generations and creating greater engagement between established legal institutions and young members of the legal community.

An important feature of the initiative will be the creation of a lasting public knowledge resource, as each edition is proposed to be professionally recorded and supported by an edited transcript and a concise ideas paper, gradually building a permanent archive of contemporary legal thought and discussion.
